facts.fact: Al-Wasat reports that Libya's national number project, aimed at a unique reference number for each citizen, has issued and circulated national numbers through a unified electronic system run by the Civil Status Authority since 2011, and that officials in 2026 were still arresting people for forging them.
Alwasat reports the civil registry's national number system is issuing national numbers, with about 1,703 forged-number cases caught from January to April 2026.
The Interior Minister of the Government of National Unity said in July 2024 that projects were adopted, chiefly an electronic ID card issuance system.
The Libyan Attorney General's Office says transfers of 61 family records between Civil Registry offices led to National Identification Numbers being issued to 225 foreign nationals of Malian origin.

facts.fact: Libya's House Defence and National Security Committee says breaches in the Civil Registry Authority let foreign nationals unlawfully obtain Libyan national ID numbers, which implies national ID numbers are being issued.
Libya's Attorney General Al-Siddiq Al-Sour said a review found more than 315,000 national identification numbers issued unlawfully, with 8,662 numbers suspended.
Technical trials of Level 3 biometric digital identity had begun with the Central Bank of Libya and a number of banks, ahead of launch and integration, per the General Information Authority.
